response: The Private Deliberation paper presents deception as an intentional behavioral strategy of the private agent: it says the agent ‘engages in private deliberation and employs deception in repeated games,’ using private reasoning to mislead opponents and improve its long-term payoff. By contrast, MAgIC treats deception as a benchmarked performance metric in Undercover/Chameleon. It defines SD as a weighted sum of success rates: SD = nwuc/nuc + λ(nwcg/ncg), where nwuc/nuc measures successful blending/wins when the model plays chameleon/undercover, and nwcg/ncg measures incorrect secret-word/code guesses, with λ = 0.25 to account for code guesses not occurring in every game. So, Private Deliberation emphasizes deception as an adversarial game-playing tactic, while MAgIC mathematically operationalizes deception as measurable success at blending in or inducing wrong guesses.
judge_justification: The response correctly contrasts the two papers: it describes Private Deliberation as promoting deception as an intentional strategy in private reasoning, and MAgIC as defining deception as a quantitative evaluation metric. It also gives the SD formula and explains its components in the Undercover/Chameleon setting, matching the reference answer’s core synthesis.
